newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriot asylum couple return home.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriot asylum couple return home.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot couple, who were reported to have sought asylum in the northern Turkish-occupied area of the divided island of Cyprus, returned home to the south on Friday saying they got lost, security sources said.

"The couple were released during the day," a spokesman for the United Nations force deployed on the island said. "We escorted them to Pergamos where they had left their car," he added, referring to a village in the southeastern area of the island where the couple entered the north earlier this week.
Turkish Cypriot police had said Iakovos Iakovou and his wife Xenia, both 24, sought asylum in the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Ankara.
Police in the southern, government-controlled areas of the island, refused to comment on the matter.
"They said they entered the occupied areas by mistake on the 18th of February and that they were not harmed by the Turks," a security source said.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia that was backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. Defections of Greek Cypriots -- 200,000 of whom were displaced to the south during the invasion -- to the northern parts of the island are virtually non-existent.
Only Ankara, which keeps some 30,000 troops in the north, recognises the Turkish Cypriot state.
